history.origins: Vazhushal (also spelled Vazhishal) is a rummy game that originated in Chennai (Tamil Nadu) and is very popular in southern India. The Tamil name means 'Wipe', referring to the distinctive rule that players may take more than one card from the discard line. It differs from Indian Rummy played further north by allowing this 'wiping' of the discard line, similar to the Western game Rummy 500.
timeline: 20th–21st century: Regional rummy variant from Chennai, popular in southern India.

setup.deck: 52 cards + jokers. A high or low (no wrap).
setup.dealing: 13 each. Discard LINE (spread out, all visible).

rules.objective: Meld all cards into valid combinations (sequences and sets) and go out first by discarding your last card; or when the stock is exhausted, win by having the highest net score (meld value minus hand value).
rules.gameplay: Draw from stock or discard LINE. Deepest card from line must form NEW meld immediately. First meld needs pure sequence. Sets (3-4 same rank) and Runs (3+ sequential same suit). Can rearrange own melds. Can't lay off on opponents. Jokers wild.
keyRules: Pure sequence required for first meld

variations.name: No negative joker
variations.description: Two-player game sometimes played without a negative joker; only printed jokers are wild, making melding harder.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes only which cards are wild; no engine constant overrides needed.

variations.name: Three players with one deck
variations.description: Three people may play with one deck (only 13 cards in stock after deal); variant limits discard line to 10 cards, moving excess to bottom of stock.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant limits discard line to 10 cards; engine overrides could be added later for line size.

scoring.winCondition: Meld all cards. Go out first.
